title: Krka Prices and 2027 Budget Guide
metaDescription: Krka National Park costs for 2027: ticket tiers, boat trips, Skradin hotels, food and transport, with daily budgets for budget, mid-range and comfort travelers.
content:
## How Much Has Krka Become More Expensive?

Krka National Park prices have risen almost every year since 2019, and the 2026 price list is the base for any 2027 plan. Adult entrance now follows three seasons: €7 from November to March, €20 in April, May and October, and €40 from June to September. Summer visitors who arrive after 15:00 pay €30. Children under 7 enter free, and ages 7–18 pay reduced rates (roughly €15 in peak season).

The jump from the winter ticket to the summer ticket is almost sixfold. Before the euro, a peak ticket was 200 kn, which is a bit over €26, so the current €40 peak price reflects a big increase. A similar step in 2027 is possible, but a decline is unlikely. Budget 5–10% above 2026 figures and check the official park webshop before booking.

## What Does Krka National Park Cost in 2027?

### Entrance tickets by season

| Period | Adult ticket | What is included |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Jun–Sep | €40 (€30 after 15:00) | Land sites, Skradin boat, Lozovac shuttle |
| Apr, May, Oct | €20 | Same |
| Nov–Mar | €7 | Land sites only, no boats |

The boat from Skradin to Skradinski buk and the shuttle bus from Lozovac run from 1 April to 31 October and are included in the ticket. The ticket covers one visit to each open land site per day. A ticket used at Lozovac cannot also be used for a boat exit from Skradin on the same day.

A cheaper ticket exists for the upstream area only (Roški slap, Burnum and nearby sites). It costs €7–€20 for adults, depending on the season.

### Boat excursions inside the park

Boat trips are charged on top of the entrance fee. The official 2026 rates for adults:

- Skradinski buk to Čikola canyon, 45 minutes: €10
- Skradinski buk to Visovac island, 2 hours: €15 (children €10)
- Visovac and Roški slap, 4 hours: €20
- Roški slap to Krka monastery and fortresses, 2 hours: €20

Visovac is worth the €15. The island holds a 15th-century Franciscan monastery and can only be reached on these boats.

## Realistic Daily Budgets for 2027

### Budget traveler: €60–€80 per person per day

This assumes a shared guesthouse room near Skradin at €60–€90 per night for two, a bus from Šibenik or Split at €10–€15 each way, one konoba meal, and a self-catered breakfast. The ticket is the swing factor. In April or October, the €20 entrance keeps the day near €60. In July, the €30 afternoon ticket helps.

### Mid-range traveler: €90–€140 per person per day

This level covers a double room at around €72–€119 per night (Hotel Vrata Krke at Lozovac and the 4-star Hotel Bonaca in Skradin sit at these levels in shoulder season), the €40 ticket, a €15 Visovac boat, and two meals at €15–€25. A rental car adds fuel and Skradin parking.

### Comfortable traveler: €150–€250 per person per day

High-end rooms in Šibenik or Skradin run €100–€250 or more per night. Private transfers and guided tours add €50–€100 or more. Summer prices are at the top of these ranges.

## Day Trip vs Overnight Stay

Organized day trips from Split, Trogir or Zadar cost about €50–€70 per person with transport, entrance and a boat ride. Some packages with extras run €60–€120. Compared with a €40 ticket plus a €10–€15 bus each way, the tour is only slightly more expensive, and it avoids parking and timetable problems.

Staying in Skradin is better for those who want to enter early. Rooms cost more in July and August, but the park opens around 08:00 and peak-day hours often run until 20:00. Early entry avoids most of the boat queues, which in August can reach 25 minutes or more.

## Lozovac vs Skradin: Which Entrance Saves Money?

Lozovac has free parking and a free shuttle bus down to the falls. This is the cheaper choice for drivers. Skradin is a riverside town where parking is paid and fills up quickly in summer. The included boat takes about 25 minutes upstream.

Most travelers overestimate the boat. In peak season, the queue can cost more time than the walk of roughly 4 km, and the ride is only a transfer. The ticket-included Lozovac shuttle is simpler. Use Skradin as a place to eat and sleep, not necessarily as the way in.

## Money-Saving Tips for Krka

- **Enter after 15:00 in summer.** The ticket drops from €40 to €30 and the heat eases. The main trails take 1.5–2 hours, so a late entry still works.
- **Choose May, early June or late September.** From April to May and in October the ticket is €20, and May offers roughly 18–25 °C with strong water flow.
- **Buy online.** The official webshop avoids ticket-office queues.
- **Winter is cheapest.** The €7 ticket is a fraction of the summer price, but boats and the Lozovac shuttle do not run, and the Lozovac entrance is the only practical way in.
- **Annual ticket.** Some listings show an annual pass at about €60. This pays off only for locals and repeat visitors.
- **Eat a block away from the Skradin waterfront.** Prices inside the park cafés and at the quay run higher than in the side streets.

## Swimming Is Not Included

Swimming in Krka has been banned for visitors since 1 January 2021. Skip any tour that advertises a swim at the falls. Tours that mention swimming typically refer to Skradin or other places outside the protected area.

## How to Get There

Krka is about 85 km from Split (roughly one hour by car). Regular bus lines run from Split, Zadar and Šibenik to Skradin (FlixBus, Liburnija, Autotrans). From Zadar, the bus ride to Skradin takes about 1 hour 20 minutes. A one-way bus from Split costs roughly €10–€15.

## What to Expect for 2027

The park has raised prices steadily since 2019, so a rise for 2027 is more likely than a freeze. The three-season structure and the afternoon discount are likely to stay. Plan around the 2026 figures, add a buffer of 5–10%, and confirm rates and boat schedules on the official park website when tickets go on sale.

faq.question: How much is the Krka National Park ticket in 2027?
faq.answer: The 2027 list has not been confirmed. The 2026 adult prices were €7 from November to March, €20 in April, May and October, and €40 from June to September. Budget a few percent more for 2027.

faq.question: Is it cheaper to visit Krka in the afternoon?
faq.answer: Yes, in summer. From June to September, adult tickets after 15:00 cost €30 instead of €40. Children, students and hiking society members pay about €11.25 at that time.

faq.question: Is the boat from Skradin included in the ticket?
faq.answer: Yes, from 1 April to 31 October. The Skradin–Skradinski buk boat and the Lozovac shuttle bus are both included. Extra excursions such as Visovac (€15) cost more.

faq.question: How much should I budget per day in Krka?
faq.answer: A budget day costs about €60–€80, a mid-range day €90–€140, and a comfortable day €150–€250 or more. Summer is at the top of each range and April or October at the bottom.

faq.question: Can you swim in Krka National Park?
faq.answer: No. Swimming has been prohibited for visitors since 1 January 2021. Plan for walking the boardwalks and visiting the viewpoints instead.

faq.question: Is a Krka day tour from Split worth the price?
faq.answer: Tours cost about €50–€70 per person, including transport, entrance and a boat ride. They are worth it for those without a car because the bus, ticket and queue time add up to a similar cost.

faq.question: Which entrance is cheaper, Lozovac or Skradin?
faq.answer: Lozovac, for drivers. Parking is free and a free shuttle runs to the falls from April to October. Skradin has paid parking that fills quickly in summer.

quickAnswer: Plan on €90–€140 per person per day in Krka for 2027 in peak summer. That covers a €40 park ticket (€30 after 15:00), a Skradin room share of €60–€120, meals at €15–€25 each, and transport. Winter is far cheaper, since tickets cost about €7. 2027 prices are estimates based on 2026 rates.
